meta.title: Session I risk register - Central Los Angeles Jack in the Box on an NNN lease
meta.method: Each risk is graded on judgement (likelihood / impact) and mapped to the four decisions the owner can actually take. Where a risk has an official measured anchor, the source is linked. Where no official anchor exists, 'Analysis' is shown and the item is listed on the Flagged for Review page.

decisions.SELL: Sell now through a Section 1031 exchange
decisions.EXTEND: Negotiate an early extension, then sell with term
decisions.HOLD: Hold to the expiry window and renew at market
decisions.EXPIRE: Let the lease expire without a renewal commitment

likelihood_definitions.High: More likely than not within the lease horizon.
likelihood_definitions.Medium: Plausible and material; roughly a 1-in-4 to 1-in-2 chance.
likelihood_definitions.Low: Unlikely in any single year but not remote over 4-9 years.

rows.risk: Term decay: every year the lease runs down, a buyer pays a wider cap rate for the same income.
rows.mitigation: Sell while at least 10 years of term remains, or convert the remaining term into a longer one through an extension.

rows.risk: Renewal is priced at market and the market rent is below in-place rent, cutting the income the asset capitalises.
rows.mitigation: Test the renewal offer against the model's 10% rent-cut case before accepting; a cut below -10% is worse than selling with term.

rows.risk: The obligor is a franchisee, not the brand: 93.0% of the Jack in the Box system is franchised, so the lease credit is a franchisee balance sheet.
rows.mitigation: Read the lease and any guaranty; obtain franchisee financials and unit-level P&L; escrow or letter of credit if the tenant asks for an extension.

rows.risk: The brand's closure programme removes units: guidance of ~2,100 restaurants including 50-60 closures in FY2026, after 86 closures in FY2025.
rows.mitigation: Ask the brand in writing whether this unit is on any closure or 'block closure' list; make the answer a condition of renewal.

rows.risk: Soft sales at the unit reduce the rent the operator can afford: system same-store sales -1.1% in Q3 FY2026 after -7.1% in the prior-year quarter.
rows.mitigation: Underwrite the store, not the brand: request unit sales, then test rent cover against a 10% sales decline.

rows.risk: Higher long rates widen cap rates: the 10-year Treasury is 4.86% and the 30-year 5.26%, so long-dated real estate capital is expensive.
rows.mitigation: A 50 bp cap-rate move is a -$270,000 swing per $100,000 NOI in the model; agree a sale timetable that does not force a sale into a spike.

rows.risk: Buyer financing: at 4.86% money and a 6.0%-7.0% cap, a leveraged buyer's spread is thin, which shrinks the bidder pool for a single-tenant asset.
rows.mitigation: Market to all-cash 1031 buyers and private capital, who are less rate-sensitive than leveraged institutions.

rows.risk: Measure ULA cliff: a City of Los Angeles sale above $5,400,000 pays a 4.0% surtax on top of the 0.45% base (5.95% at $10.9m).
rows.mitigation: Model the price against the indexed threshold; where the price is near it, structure or time the sale so the surtax does not apply, and take advice before signing.

rows.risk: Proposition 13 reassessment on sale resets the buyer's base-year value to market, so the buyer's property tax rises permanently and the price falls by the capitalised amount.
rows.mitigation: Show buyers the post-sale tax bill; price expectations must already reflect it.

rows.risk: Wage regulation compresses franchisee margins: $20.00 fast-food minimum wage and a $18.42 City minimum wage, both indexed, with the Fast Food Council able to raise the former.
rows.mitigation: Stress the tenant's rent cover at a 5% wage increase; a tenant who cannot cover is not a renewal candidate.

rows.risk: Input-cost inflation: LA metro CPI-U is +3.7% with food +2.8% and energy +20.3%, the costs a restaurant operator faces first.
rows.mitigation: Tie any extension to escalations at or above CPI, not below it.

rows.risk: Insurance cost and availability: a 60% 30-year chance of an M>=6.7 quake in the region keeps earthquake cover expensive and can make it unobtainable.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a current bound quote and the earthquake deductible before any decision; check whether the lease makes the tenant responsible for insurance.

rows.risk: Re-tenanting risk: a drive-thru box is not re-lettable like inline retail; a new use may need a new conditional-use permit.
rows.mitigation: Never let the lease expire without a signed renewal or a signed replacement tenant; budget 18 months of vacancy and 5% of value in re-leasing cost.

rows.risk: Zoning and permitting: continued drive-thru use depends on the site's conditional-use entitlement and current City rules.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a zoning report and the CUP history before underwriting a re-let. Not verified in this workbook.

rows.risk: Section 1031 execution risk: 45 days to identify and 180 days to close, through a qualified intermediary; missing either makes the whole gain taxable.
rows.mitigation: Line up the intermediary and replacement candidates before listing; identify more than one replacement property; never take constructive receipt.

rows.risk: Liquidity: a single-tenant QSR is a small, specialised asset with a narrow buyer pool, so a forced sale is a discount sale.
rows.mitigation: Market for 6-9 months off-market and on-market; avoid any deadline that forces a quick close.

rows.risk: Environmental liability: a decades-old restaurant site can carry soil or groundwater impact, and a buyer will require a Phase I and possibly a Phase II.
rows.mitigation: Commission a Phase I ESA before going to market; price the timing into the sale plan.

rows.risk: Population decline: the official state projection has Los Angeles County falling from 9,811,358 in 2026 to 9,637,524 in 2040 (-1.8%).
rows.mitigation: Population is a slow variable and the trade area is dense (8,304 persons per sq mi in the City); do not let it drive the decision, but do not assume growth either.

rows.risk: Seismic retrofit exposure: unreinforced masonry or non-ductile concrete buildings face mandatory retrofit obligations and tenant disruption.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a structural and seismic assessment. Building type is unknown to this workbook.

rows.risk: Major earthquake. The official 30-year probabilities for the Los Angeles region are 60% for M>=6.7, 46% for M>=7.0 and 31% for M>=7.5.
rows.mitigation: Physically: retrofit and insure, including business-interruption and ordinance-or-law cover. Financially: a sale removes the tail from the owner's balance sheet, and a Section 1031 into several properties diversifies it across locations.

rows.risk: Urban fire or smoke event: CAL FIRE classifies hazard by parcel into Moderate, High and Very High zones, and the January 2025 Los Angeles fires showed that a metropolitan fire can destroy thousands of structures.
rows.mitigation: Look the address up in the FHSZ viewer and the local responsibility area map; confirm insurance is not dependent on a state-run insurer of last resort. Parcel class is unverified here.

rows.risk: Pandemic or public-health closure order removing dine-in and drive-thru trade for months.
rows.mitigation: Lease language on abatement and business interruption; rent deposit; a sale at a tight cap transfers this risk to a diversified buyer.

rows.risk: Brand or franchisee insolvency: the issuer carries $1.47 billion of debt against a $901 million stockholders' deficit and has suspended its dividend.
rows.mitigation: Guaranty and security deposit; monitor the issuer's 10-Q each quarter; treat a covenant breach or a going-concern note as a sell trigger.

rows.risk: Insurer withdrawal or assessment: carriers can non-renew a book, and the state insurer of last resort can levy assessments on policyholders.
rows.mitigation: Test a 2x premium and a $100,000 deductible in the cash-flow model; if the tenant pays insurance under the NNN, confirm it actually does.

rows.risk: Flood or extreme storm with the flood zone unknown at parcel level.
rows.mitigation: Look the address up in the FEMA Flood Map Service Center; buy flood cover where required.

rows.risk: Civil disturbance closing a Central Los Angeles block for weeks, or physically damaging the storefront.
rows.mitigation: Insurance and a tenant with operating depth; a diversified replacement portfolio does not remove this but spreads it.

rows.risk: An employment shock concentrated in one sector: Information employment is already -5.7% year over year in the metro.
rows.mitigation: Check the trade area's dependence on a single employer or sector before renewing; the metro is diversified across health, leisure and trade.

rows.risk: Water or power restriction that interrupts restaurant operations or raises operating costs.
rows.mitigation: Operational resilience is the tenant's problem under an NNN lease; the owner's exposure is vacancy if the tenant fails.

rows.risk: Policy shock: a new or expanded transfer tax, rent regulation, or a change to Section 1031 or Proposition 13.
rows.mitigation: Measure ULA shows how fast City transaction costs can move: 0.45% base plus a 4%-5.5% surtax above the threshold. Execute the sale while current rules are known rather than after a change.

rows.risk: Rate shock: a sustained move in the 10-year Treasury well above today's 4.86% re-prices every cap rate.
rows.mitigation: Do not sell into a spike; if the plan requires a sale, pre-negotiate and keep a hold alternative that still cash-flows.

rows.risk: Land value collapse in the trade area from a localised event that removes foot traffic permanently.
rows.mitigation: Diversification through a Section 1031 exchange into several markets is the only structural hedge available to a single-asset owner.
